An '''academic degree''' is a qualification awarded by a [[University|university]]
or other [[Higher education|higher-education institution]] on completion of a
course of study. Degrees are organised in ascending levels, principally the
undergraduate bachelor's degree and the postgraduate master's degree and
doctorate.<ref name="wp-deg" />

== Levels ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Level !! Character
|-
| Bachelor's || The most common undergraduate qualification; provides foundational knowledge and broad entry to careers or further study.<ref name="wp-deg" /><ref name="research" />
|-
| Master's || A postgraduate degree offering advanced specialisation and a more concentrated, rigorous curriculum.<ref name="research" />
|-
| Doctorate || The highest academic qualification; centred on original research culminating in a dissertation, and oriented toward expert and leadership roles.<ref name="ebsco" /><ref name="research" />
|}

Some systems also recognise shorter undergraduate awards (such as the associate
or foundation degree) below the bachelor's level.<ref name="wp-deg" />

== International reference scale ==

International frameworks place these awards on a common scale: sub-bachelor's
higher education, bachelor's level, master's level and doctoral level occupy the
successive upper tiers.<ref name="wp-he" />
